chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'May Allah be Merciful upon a servant who seeks a need from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, so he is insistent in the supplication, whether it is Answered for him or not Answered for him.'
And he recited this Verse: 'And I will call upon my Lord, perhaps I shall not remain unblessed in calling upon my Lord.'

key_terms.أَلَحَّ: To be insistent, persistent, or earnest in supplication
key_terms.اسْتُجِيبَ: It was answered (passive form of istijabah)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of persistence in prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the spiritual virtue of 'al-alah' (earnest persistence) in supplication, teaching that the act of persistent asking itself is a source of divine mercy, regardless of whether the request is granted immediately or delayed. It underscores the Shia scholarly understanding that the supplicant’s confidence in Allah’s mercy remains intact even if the specific outcome is deferred, as illustrated by the Prophet’s recitation of Quran 19:48. This principle encourages believers to maintain hope and continuity in their connection with the Divine, viewing delay not as rejection but as a form of answered prayer.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> be Merciful upon a servant who seeks a need from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, so he is insistent in the supplication, whether is it Answered for him or not Answered for him’;
and heasws recited this Verse [19:48] And I will withdraw from you and what you call on besides Allah, and I will call upon my Lord, perhaps I shall not remain unblessed in calling upon my Lord’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Ash’ari from ibn al-Qaddah from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘May Allah grant favors upon a servant who requests help from Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, and insists on praying and pleading before Him for help, accepted or not.
He then read this verse of the Holy Quran: “. . . I worship my Lord and hope that my prayers will not be ignored.’” [19:48]
